reason: 'cleft 1/4-1/3 to midrib' is a ratio: the depth (PATO_0001595) of the leaf sinus (PO_0025384) as a fraction of the distance from the margin to the midrib. It is not a quality term. The perianth example ('cerca de 1 tercio') is a fragment that has lost its second term.
'Tinged' means the colour is faint or only partly present. It becomes an approximate qualifier with 'tinged' as its cue (docs/odp/01-approximate-value.md); the value is lilac.
A measurement of length (PATO_0000122) on the corolla lip (FLOPO_0985017). The lip carries the position lower (FLOPO:0991377), because in a corolla the abaxial lip is the lower one.

A transcription fragment: the prefix of 'uni- or bipinnatisect' cut off by its suspended hyphen. It should be expanded to 'unipinnatisect or bipinnatisect' and read as alternatives (docs/odp/07-alternatives.md).

'Horn' is a generic outgrowth with no PO or FLOPO class, so it needs the organ it belongs to, like 'appendage' in the previous review. The presence of horns is already covered by horned (FLOPO:0991029).
'Many-flowered' is an indefinite count of flowers (amount 'many'). 'Laxly' adds a second statement on the inflorescence: loose (PATO_0001802), following the earlier rule for 'lax'.
The scale or bract has an awn (PO_0025349), and the awn is scabrous (FLOPO:0991058). That is a quality of a part of the bearer, not a quality of its own.
'Paniculate' says that the inflorescence is a panicle, which is a kind of part, not a quality. 'Broadly' is a vague width modifier and is dropped.
To disarticulate is to fall off at a joint; FLOPO already uses PATO_0001730 for the shed part (fugacious FLOPO:0991231). 'Not disarticulate' is its negation, and 'in fruit' is a stage.

A distance (PATO_0000040) between the opposite leaf sinuses (PO_0025384) of a lobed blade, which is the spacing case of a relation to a part of the same kind. 'Widest' picks one pair of sinuses; it is not a quality.
Two values of different attributes. The bearer is puberulous (FLOPO:0991049), and its hairs (trichome PO_0000282) are retrorse (PATO_0002237).

This is length (PATO_0000122) of the exospore of the plant spore (PO_0025017), a measurement and not a new quality. The exospore needs a FLOPO anatomy class beside perispore (FLOPO_0986069) before these rows can be grounded.

label: baculate
definition: A surface feature shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's surface bearing rod-shaped projections that are longer than broad and blunt, not pointed. NOTE: Palynological term for spore and pollen ornament. It is a sibling of spiny (PATO_0001365) and close to warty (PATO_0001361).
reason: A standard term for perispore and megaspore ornament that PATO lacks. The 'stamen: baculate' rows look mis-transcribed and should be checked.
Every example is a bamboo culm-sheath apex that is cut off at a slant along one side, which is what obliquely truncate means.

target: new: conjunction of two values of different attributes
reason: The veins are both curved (PATO_0000406, the earlier rule for 'arcuate') and ascending (PATO_0104355). These are a shape and an orientation, so this is two statements and not a continuum between values.
Antiphyllous inflorescences and cymes are those that arise opposite a leaf.

label: supramedial
definition: A positional quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being located beyond the middle of the structure that bears it, between the middle and its apex or margin. NOTE: Sibling of median (FLOPO:0991381), which is the middle member of a series; used for the position of sori between the costa and the margin, and of wings on fruits.
reason: Sorus position (medial, supramedial, inframedial) is a common fern character, and FLOPO has only median.
'Almost' / 'presque' is an approximation cue (docs/odp/01-approximate-value.md) on the value free.
'Silky' / 'soyeux' is an exact synonym of sericeous. 'Densely' is a degree word and stays in the record.
The hairs of the bearer (trichome PO_0000282) are erect (PATO_0000622). This is a quality of a part of the bearer.
'Anastomosées vers le bord' says that the veins rejoin one another, which is anastomosing.
An angular stem or rachis whose angles are obtuse. There is no angle bearer to carry 'obtuse', so the obtuse refinement stays in the record words.
'Without petals' or 'lack petals' is the absence of petals (docs/odp/15-absence-of-a-part.md).
This is the colour of the glands (portion of secretory tissue PO_0005656) on the bearer. Each colour word grounds to its own colour value.
The lower bracts are linear and blade-like, as opposed to reduced to a point ('or acuminate'). 'Laminate' adds nothing that has a reliable term of its own.
An OCR or spelling error for scarious; the bearers are bracts, phyllaries and chaff.
'Bigeminate' means twice paired: two pairs of stipules or stipels, a count of pairs (has member). The single pair is the rule geminate → paired (FLOPO:0991004).
The cypsela margins bear calluses, which is callose with 'calloused' as a synonym. 'Thin' only modifies how thick the callus is, and the margin is the part of the bearer.
